newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-MMC prolongs the agony for Sears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-MMC prolongs the agony for Sears.

text.p: British retailer Sears Plc's efforts to sell its Freemans home shopping arm hit another snag on Wednesday as the country's monopoly watchdog demanded more time to investigate the deal.
Sears shares sank as investors saw prospects of a promised payout from the 367.5 million pound ($616.1 million) sale of Freemans to Littlewoods recede further.

The request by the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) to extend the deadline for its report on Freemans by two months became the latest setback for Sears' attempts to sell Freemans as part of a broader restructuring to improve returns for shareholders.
The British government agreed to give the MMC until September 22 to complete its work after the watchdog asked for more time because of the complexity of the merger.
The MMC had been due to give its verdict to the Department of Trade and Industry on Monday.
In April Sears, whose retail empires includes department store Selfridges, announced plans to sell its Freemans home shopping business to football pools-to-home shopping firm Littlewoods.
The deal was referred to the MMC on grounds that it would give Littlewoods around 25 percent of the UK mail order market.
The sale of Freemans formed part of a sweeping reorganisation of Sears' retail empire, including the demerger of Selfridges and rationalisation of its loss-making British Shoe Corporation.
Sears promised to hand proceeds from the Freemans sale back to shareholders, if it got a green light from the government.
Retail analysts said the delay would effectively mean no decision on Freemans until November, pushing back prospects of a cash payout to investors into next year.
"The chances of a payout in calendar 1997 look increasingly remote," said one retail sector analyst.
Sears shares fell 2.5 pence to 62.5 pence.
Analysts said there was at best a 50/50 chance that the government would approve the merger.
"If it's disallowed it would be another mess for Sears," said Nick Bubb, retail analyst at SocGen.
The Freemans deal has become a long-running saga of misfortune for the retailer.
Littlewoods originally agreed to buy Freemans in January for 395 million pounds, but Sears switched to rival mail order group N.Brown when the merger with Littlewoods was referred to the MMC.
N.Brown pulled out after negotations with Sears foundered over the price, Littlewoods returned as the buyer and the MMC probe was reinstated.

The shake-up of Sears, which included the departure of chief executive Liam Strong, aimed to improve returns for investors, who had grown increasingly dissatisfied with the firms' dismal record on profits and share price underperformance.

Selfridges, worth an estimated 500 million pounds, is likely to be demerged and floated next summer and "company doctor" David Jones, hired to sort out British Shoe, is due to report to the board in September. ($ = 0.596 British Pounds)
